implementedControls.nativeStartup: firebase_performance_collection_deactivated is literal true under every Android main application and boolean true under every used iOS Runner plist. All app/src Android manifests are checked for contradictory/duplicate overrides.
implementedControls.bootstrap: New and already initialized native Firebase paths request Performance collection false. General observability no longer enables Performance. A setter failure preserves initialized best effort startup and the next bootstrap retries disabling. Web guard preserved.
implementedControls.finiteTelemetry: Existing closed Analytics/Crashlytics/operational-health telemetry remains governed by its existing finite contracts; no new custom traces, HTTP metrics, dependencies or SDK versions introduced.
implementedControls.ciVerifier: verify_native_controls(root, scopes) returns ten source-bound target records; NativeControlError extends ValueError and retains a finite structured report. CLI derives the real declared five-club release scope.

findings.finding: Installed native SDK URL redaction retains arbitrary private path segments.
findings.evidence: Actual installed SDK utility strips userinfo/query/fragment but preserves /orders/opaque_private_supporter_alias on a synthetic URL. Invalid URL parsing also returns the original string. This is a raw URL utility proof, not a live automatic trace or backend transmission.

findings.finding: Native HTTP metric construction stores the URL after that redaction and length truncation.
Installed collection resolution checks permanent deactivation first, then persisted collection choice before manifest default.
findings.note: A default enabled=false flag or skipping the setter does not override a previously persisted true. Permanent deactivation returns disabled before those choices.

findings.finding: Installed runtime setter cannot enable permanently deactivated Performance.
findings.note: When permanently deactivated, the Android setter returns before writing persisted collection state; local proof claims a false request and permanent override, not erasure of old SDK cache values.

findings.finding: Native Performance transport includes an SDK installation identifier outside the app finite diagnostic payload contract.
findings.note: The method obtains FirebaseInstallationsApi.getId and writes ApplicationInfo.appInstanceId when enabled. This is an SDK identifier, not proof of a business user ID or of any actual transmission.

findings.finding: Installed Apple Flutter setter forwards only dataCollectionEnabled, while automatic instrumentation has a separate native control.
findings.note: The installed Swift wrapper61–64 only changes isDataCollectionEnabled. Official Apple guidance distinguishes that custom collection setting from isInstrumentationEnabled for automatic monitoring, and documents permanent plist deactivation.

documentedControlSemantics.claim: Permanent Android deactivation overrides normal collection choice and cannot be reversed by a runtime enable call; library reporting and Gradle instrumentation are separate controls.
Permanent plist deactivation blocks runtime reenablement. Automatic instrumentation and custom data collection are distinct Apple properties.

retainedEvidence.firstFullCheckpointDescription: Runtime/package/enabled SDK/control/mutation checks passed; retained startup indentation assertion failed31/1 combined, and strict found one unnecessary test import. Both test-only corrections are included in the corrected current receipt.

coverageBeforeFix.description: Source assertions checked collection defaults/general gating, not actual Performance channel payloads or permanent controls across five hosts.
coverageBeforeFix.note: Those fixtures initialize Core directly and exercised Analytics/Crashlytics, bypassing FirebaseBootstrapService and the Performance channel.
